title_en: AI Claims Force Review of Prize-Winning Microscope Video
title_zh: AI争议促使尼康复核获奖显微视频
summary_zh: 尼康正在重新评估其年度显微摄影比赛 `Small World In Motion` 的获奖视频，原因是其他科学家质疑该视频可能由人工智能（`AI`）生成或被改动。获奖视频由清华大学研究员 `Dr Ning Xu` 提交，他否认使用 `AI` 生成实验影像、纤毛或其运动，仅承认在重建灰度图像时用 `AI` 区分和可视化特征。多位研究人员及两位前评委对画面中结构突然出现或消失、疑似带有 `AI` 水印等问题提出担忧。尼康表示目前尚不认为有规则被违反，但将很快公布更新；此事之所以重要，是因为该比赛对科学影像的真实性和生成式 `AI` 的使用有明确限制。
reading_passage:
Watch: The competition's winner and runners up. Nikon is investigating whether the winning video (shown left) was altered with AI

The winning entry of a prestigious scientific photography competition is being re-evaluated following criticism from other scientists that it was made with AI.

Nikon's annual Small World In Motion contest accepts photos and video taken using powerful microscopes, and has run annually for the last 15 years.

The winner was a short video submitted by Dr Ning Xu, a researcher at Tsinghua University in China, which claims to be footage of tiny, hair-like structures called cilia moving inside the airways of a child with a rare disease.

Xu did not respond to the BBC's request for comment, but has posted online denying he broke the competition rules.

In a response to a post by Nikon on LinkedIn, external, he did not dispute using AI within the image processing but said he remained within the rules of the contest.

"AI was not used to generate the experimental movie, the cilia, or their motion," he said.

Xu's video is artificially brightly coloured - common in microscopy and permitted in the contest - which is usually done manually using stains and dyes on the sample itself.

He accepted AI was used "to distinguish and visualize features in the reconstructed grayscale images".

But the challenges made by other scientists include claims that the video contains shapes and movements which did not fit with normal cell structures or behaviours, and that the cilia seemed to be too big.

Commenting on Nikon's social media post, Edward Phelps, associate professor at Florida University, observed some of the structures "pop in and out of existence" and the cilia "appear from nowhere".

Meanwhile PhD student Ian Donovan from UT Southwestern Medical Centre said the source image appeared to contain a distinctive watermark indicating it had been AI generated.

Additionally, two former competition judges said they also had concerns about whether the image was real.

Nikon said Xu was "respectfully complying" with its investigation and had provided it with additional technical documents.

Dr Patrick Hickey, who came fifth in the 2026 Small World contest, said the recognition the award represents means more than the $3,000 (£2,250) prize itself.

"If you spend a lot of your time in a dark room looking down a microscope, it's really nice to be able to show people and to show the public," he said.

"There's an interesting fusion between science and art, and a lot of the images that scientists are making have some very abstract and artistic qualities to them."

Hickey said it would be unfair on other entrants if it turned out the winning video was unfairly altered by AI.

"There's a specific set of rules in the contest, and one of them was quite clearly that you couldn't use generative AI to produce things, and the other was obviously that it has to be taken under a microscope," he said.

So far, Nikon is standing by its procedures but it said there would be an update soon.

"At this time, we don't see that any rules were violated," it said in a statement.

vocabulary.example: She won a prestigious grant to study cell movement.
Cilia help move mucus out of the airways.
All entrants must comply with the contest guidelines.
The image carried a distinctive digital watermark.
The judges checked whether generative AI had been used to create the video.
Image processing can make microscopic details easier to see.
The software assembled the scans into a single grayscale image.
The organisers said they stood by their initial review of the entry.
It turned out that the watermark had been added by editing software.
The team compared the original scan with the reconstructed image.

difficult_sentences.sentence: The winning entry of a prestigious scientific photography competition is being re-evaluated following criticism from other scientists that it was made with AI.
difficult_sentences.explanation_zh: 主句为 “The winning entry ... is being re-evaluated”，其中 `is being re-evaluated` 为现在进行时被动语态；“following criticism ...” 为介词短语说明事件发生的原因；“that it was made with AI” 是 `criticism` 的同位语从句，说明批评的具体内容。
difficult_sentences.grammar_point: 现在进行时被动语态；criticism 后的同位语从句
difficult_sentences.translation_zh: 该项久负盛名的科学摄影比赛的获奖作品因其他科学家批评其由人工智能制作而正被重新评估。

difficult_sentences.sentence: The winner was a short video submitted by Dr Ning Xu, a researcher at Tsinghua University in China, which claims to be footage of tiny, hair-like structures called cilia moving inside the airways of a child with a rare disease.
difficult_sentences.explanation_zh: 主句为 “The winner was a short video”；“submitted by Dr Ning Xu” 是过去分词短语作后置定语；“a researcher at Tsinghua University in China” 是 `Dr Ning Xu` 的同位语；“which claims to be footage ...” 是非限制性定语从句修饰 `video`；“called cilia” 是过去分词短语修饰 `structures`；“moving inside ...” 是现在分词短语作 `cilia` 的定语。
difficult_sentences.grammar_point: 非限制性定语从句；多重分词后置定语
difficult_sentences.translation_zh: 获奖作品是中国清华大学研究员 `Dr Ning Xu` 提交的一段短视频，该视频声称拍到一个患有罕见疾病的儿童气道内被称为纤毛的微小毛发状结构的运动。

difficult_sentences.sentence: Commenting on Nikon's social media post, Edward Phelps, associate professor at Florida University, observed some of the structures 'pop in and out of existence' and the cilia 'appear from nowhere'.
difficult_sentences.explanation_zh: 主句为 “Edward Phelps ... observed some of the structures 'pop in and out of existence' and the cilia 'appear from nowhere'”；句首 “Commenting on Nikon's social media post” 为现在分词短语作状语，其逻辑主语为 `Edward Phelps`；“associate professor at Florida University” 是 `Edward Phelps` 的同位语；两处引号内容分别作 `observed` 的宾语。
difficult_sentences.grammar_point: 现在分词短语作状语；引语作宾语
difficult_sentences.translation_zh: 佛罗里达大学副教授爱德华·费尔普斯在评论尼康的社交媒体帖子时指出，一些结构“时隐时现”，纤毛“凭空出现”。

difficult_sentences.sentence: "There's a specific set of rules in the contest, and one of them was quite clearly that you couldn't use generative AI to produce things, and the other was obviously that it has to be taken under a microscope," he said.
difficult_sentences.explanation_zh: 主句可视为 `he said`，引语中 “There's a specific set of rules in the contest” 为第一层主句；后用 `and` 连接两个表语从句说明具体规则：“one of them was quite clearly that you couldn't use generative AI to produce things” 和 “the other was obviously that it has to be taken under a microscope”。
difficult_sentences.grammar_point: 并列复合句；that 引导的表语从句
difficult_sentences.translation_zh: 他说：“比赛有一套明确的规则，其中一条非常清楚：不能使用生成式人工智能来生成内容；另一条显然是被拍摄对象必须在显微镜下拍摄。”

idioms.expression: pop in and out of existence
idioms.meaning_zh: 突然出现又消失；时隐时现
idioms.usage_note: 非正式、形象化的固定表达，常用于描述数字画面或本应稳定的对象异常地断续出现，多带质疑或批评语气。
idioms.example: In the edited video, several particles seemed to pop in and out of existence.

idioms.meaning_zh: 凭空出现；不知从哪里冒出来
idioms.usage_note: 口语化固定短语，强调出现没有可见来源或前兆；在报道中用来质疑视频内容不符合正常细胞行为。
idioms.example: The watermark appeared from nowhere in the final frame.

idioms.usage_note: 中性固定短语，常与现在完成时或一般现在时连用，说明某一状态尚未改变。
idioms.example: So far, no rules appear to have been broken.

options.A: A scientist who admitted to using AI in a microscopy contest.
options.B: A review of a winning microscope video after claims that it may have been AI-generated.
options.C: Nikon's decision to cancel a photography competition over AI concerns.
options.D: The growing role of AI in scientific image processing.

reading_questions.question: What does the Nikon Small World In Motion contest accept?

options.A: Only still photographs taken with standard cameras.
options.D: Photos and video taken using powerful microscopes.

options.A: The video was made without any human involvement.
options.B: The cilia were generated completely by AI.
options.C: The disease shown is common in children.
options.D: The footage was intended to show cilia moving in a child's airways.

reading_questions.question: In paragraph 2, the word 're-evaluated' is closest in meaning to:

options.A: As final and unwilling to reconsider.
options.B: As confident but leaving room for an update.
options.C: As critical of the scientists' complaints.
options.D: As indifferent to the contest rules.

options.A: It introduces a controversy, gives supporting claims and responses, and ends with current status.
options.B: It presents a sequence of events leading to a final verdict.
